If you could turn back time to the early days of the internet, would you handle privacy differently? Most of us would think so: we would be more cautious about the services we join and the information we share. But time machines don't exist, and we have to face reality — your personal data is already out there right now, being traded and sold.

At this very moment, your phone number, email address, home address, and even your family relationships are being packaged and sold to marketers, insurance companies, and hackers. While privacy protection features in Safari and Mail can block some tracking as you browse the web, they cannot erase information that has been collected over the years and scattered across hundreds of broker databases. Data brokers have built a multi-billion-dollar industry by collecting your digital footprints, packaging them up, and selling them on. It's time to pull your personal data out of the market and off the internet. Let's see how.

The security risks of the data broker industry

However, the danger goes far beyond annoying spam calls. When your data is everywhere, you become an easy target for sophisticated cyber threats. Since the industry is essentially unregulated, your most private information and details — including past jobs and residences, previous loan records, and more — can be purchased with ease. This creates a massive security risk.

Modern scammers use broker data to gather and carefully craft highly personalised (and hard-to-spot) phishing attacks. When scammers already know your job title, past addresses, or the names of your colleagues and friends, they can easily break through your instinctive defences. If a scammer knows a great deal about you and strikes when your guard is at its lowest, their chances of success rise sharply.

For those concerned about personal safety, these websites and brokers function like open search databases, becoming tools for stalkers. By mapping the network of relationships between your relatives and neighbours, brokers provide a blueprint for locating anyone who wants to stay under the radar and keep a low profile.

The solution: use Incogni to automatically remove your data

The scale of this ecosystem is staggering and, frankly, disheartening. Requesting the removal of your data from hundreds of sites one by one is a full-time job with a near-zero success rate — because if it were easy, these brokers would have gone out of business long ago. What you need is a solution that deeply understands the ins and outs of this industry and can help you reclaim your right to privacy.

This is exactly why a service like Incogni is essential to your life, both in the digital world and the real one. It takes the enormous problem you face — your data being everywhere and being sold — and turns it into a solved problem with a one-stop solution. Incogni handles the repetitive, tedious bureaucratic back-and-forth of opt-out requests on your behalf, so you don't have to spend months tracking down data brokers one by one. They make sure your data isn't just deleted once, but stays deleted, preventing brokers — who inevitably try to — from re-collecting and re-importing your information.

Incogni's comprehensive dashboard lets you track the progress of your data removals in real time, including:

  • The number of databases that may hold your information

The real-world benefits of data removal for the privacy-conscious

Clearing your information from internet broker databases delivers immediate results for you and your family

  • When companies can't buy your number, scam calls and spam texts drop.
  • Scammers lose their targets. Identity thieves typically pull victim information straight from broker sites.
  • Your personal address stays private, making it hard for stalkers to easily find where you live.
  • Your credit score stays healthy, because less data exposure reduces the risk of identity theft and strengthens your overall financial well-being.
